the extent of over/underpricing of IPOs is not significantly correlated or associated with the economic condition of Malaysia and Market Sentiments.
the extent of IPO underpricing in Malaysia has decreased over the period of 2001 to 2010.
the extent of the underpricing of IPO has decreased compared to the previous years, and there is no clear trend of the underpricing or overpricing of IPOs.

identifying the impact of economic conditions, market sentiments and financial variables on IPOs.
the impact of economic, financial and market sentiments on initial return of IPOs.

identifying the impact of economic, market sentiments and accounting indicators on the under/over pricing of IPOs and the findings of this study are expected to be beneficial to both investors and issuers of IPOs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the underpricing of IPO has decreased significantly and the extent of overpricing has increased slightly over the period 1990 2010.
the underpricing of IPO is not significantly influenced by economic conditions, market sentiments or accounting indicators.
there is no clear evidence to suggest that economic factors and market sentiments play a significant role in determining the initial returns of an IPO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extent of over and underpricing has been reduced and there isn't a clear trend for over/underpricing of IPOs for 2001 to 2010.

the extent of over and under pricing of IPOs have been significantly reduced compared to the 1980s and 1990s and that there isn't a clear trend in the extent of overpricing and underpricing for the period of 2001 2009 except for 2009 where the extent of over pricing of 15.9% was observed.

there is a significant relationship between the market sentiment (turnover) and the under pricing of IPOs, whilst the economic factors, market sentiment, and accounting indicators do not significantly impact on the initial returns of an IPO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the market sentiments (Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index and Turnover), economic condition and financial indicators have little impact on the initial pricing of IPOs.
there are no clear trends or patterns that could be used to predict the underpricing of IPO.
the extent of over/ under pricing is more dependent on the company's fundamentals rather than economic factors and market sentiments.
